jp: 誰[だれ]もいないのに、部屋[へや]の電気[でんき]が{ついています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Nobody is there, yet the light in the room is on.
why: The light is simply on, with no one arranging it, so the intransitive ついている fits.

jp: 事故[じこ]で、電車[でんしゃ]が駅[えき]に{止[と]まっています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Because of an accident, the train is stopped at the station.
why: The train is stopped by itself (が, no one acting), so the intransitive 止まっている describes the state.

jp: 道[みち]に誰[だれ]かの財布[さいふ]が{落[お]ちている|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Someone's wallet is lying on the road.
why: Nobody put the wallet there on purpose; it is just in the fallen state, so 落ちている.

jp: ボールが当[あ]たって、窓[まど]ガラスが{割[わ]れています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: A ball hit it, and the window pane is broken.
why: The pane broke by accident and is now in a broken state, so the intransitive 割れている is used.

jp: このシャツは、ソースで{汚[よご]れています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: This shirt is stained with sauce.
why: The shirt got dirty without anyone intending it, so the intransitive 汚れている describes the state.

jp: このエアコンは{壊[こわ]れています|tr-teiru-tearu}から、使[つか]えません。
en: This air conditioner is broken, so you can't use it.
why: The machine is in a broken state with no agent in view, so 壊れている, not the transitive 壊す.

jp: あそこの席[せき]が{空[あ]いています|tr-teiru-tearu}よ。座[すわ]りましょう。
en: That seat over there is vacant. Let's sit down.
why: The seat is simply empty, so the intransitive 空いている; 空ける would need someone acting.

jp: 雨[あめ]で、道[みち]が{濡[ぬ]れています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The road is wet from the rain.
why: The rain made the road wet by itself; the resulting state is the intransitive 濡れている.

jp: コートのボタンが一[ひと]つ{取[と]れている|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: One button has come off the coat.
why: The button came off by itself and the coat is now in that state, so 取れている.

jp: 子供[こども]が遊[あそ]んだので、部屋[へや]が{散[ち]らかっています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The children played, so the room is a mess.
d: 散[ち]らかしてあります
散[ち]らかっておきます
why: The room is the subject (が) and is in a messy state, so the intransitive 散らかっている.

jp: 家[いえ]の前[まえ]に、人[ひと]がたくさん{集[あつ]まっています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: A lot of people are gathered in front of the house.
d: 集[あつ]まっておきます
why: The people gathered of their own accord, so the intransitive 集まっている describes the state.

jp: 台風[たいふう]で、道[みち]に大[おお]きな木[き]が{倒[たお]れている|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Because of the typhoon, a big tree is lying across the road.
why: The wind knocked the tree down and it now lies there, so the intransitive 倒れている.

jp: この本[ほん]は、ページが{破[やぶ]れています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: A page of this book is torn.
why: The page is in a torn state (が, no agent), so the intransitive 破れている.

jp: リモコンの電池[でんち]が{切[き]れている|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The batteries in the remote are dead.
why: The batteries ran out by themselves; the resulting state is expressed with 切れている.

jp: 天気[てんき]がいいので、洗濯物[せんたくもの]がもう{乾[かわ]いています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The weather is nice, so the laundry is already dry.
d: 乾[かわ]かしてあります
why: The laundry dried by itself, so the intransitive 乾いている describes its present state.

jp: 風[かぜ]で、ドアが少[すこ]し{開[あ]いています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The door has blown slightly open in the wind.
why: The wind opened it; nobody did it on purpose, so the intransitive 開いている, not 開けてある.

jp: 公園[こうえん]の桜[さくら]が{咲[さ]いている|tr-teiru-tearu}ね。
en: The cherry blossoms in the park are in bloom, aren't they?
why: Blossoms open by themselves, so the result state is 咲いている; てある needs a deliberate agent.

jp: 停電[ていでん]で、廊下[ろうか]の電気[でんき]が{消[き]えています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Because of the power failure, the hallway light is off.
why: The light went out through the power failure, no one switched it off, so 消えている.

jp: 駅[えき]の窓口[まどぐち]に、学生[がくせい]が{並[なら]んでいます|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Students are lined up at the station ticket window.
why: The students take their own places in line, so the intransitive 並んでいる.

jp: このスプーンが{曲[ま]がっています|tr-teiru-tearu}ね。
en: This spoon is bent, isn't it?
why: The spoon is in a bent state with が and no agent, so the intransitive 曲がっている.

jp: 急[いそ]いで！もう授業[じゅぎょう]が{始[はじ]まっている|tr-teiru-tearu}よ。
en: Hurry! Class has already started.
why: The class has begun and is now under way; with が and no agent this is 始まっている.

jp: 足[あし]のけがが、もう{治[なお]っていますか|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Has your leg injury already healed?
why: The injury heals by itself (が), and the question asks about its present state, so 治っている.

jp: 姉[あね]は京都[きょうと]に{住[す]んでいます|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: My older sister lives in Kyoto.
why: A continuing present state of living somewhere is expressed with ている; てある needs a prepared object.

jp: その歌[うた]を{知[し]っています|tr-teiru-tearu}か。
en: Do you know that song?
why: Knowing is a state that continues, so 知っている; the plain 知ります would mean coming to know.

jp: 田中[たなか]さんは、もう{結婚[けっこん]しています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Mr. Tanaka is already married.
d: 結婚[けっこん]してあります
結婚[けっこん]しておきます
結婚[けっこん]しません
why: Being married is a continuing state, so 結婚している; the other forms are ungrammatical or mean something else.

jp: 夜[よる]なので、銀行[ぎんこう]のドアが{閉[し]まっています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: It is night, so the bank's door is closed.
why: The door is shut (が, intransitive), describing the present state, so 閉まっている.

jp: 空[そら]に、月[つき]が{出[で]ています|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The moon is out in the sky.
why: The moon has come out by itself and is now visible, so the intransitive 出ている.

jp: 久[ひさ]しぶりに帰[かえ]ると、町[まち]がすっかり{変[か]わっていました|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: When I went back after a long time, the town had completely changed.
d: 変[か]わっておきました
why: The town itself is the subject (が) and had ended up in a changed state, so 変わっていた.

jp: ラーメンがもう{冷[さ]めています|tr-teiru-tearu}よ。早[はや]く食[た]べて。
en: The ramen has already gone cold. Eat it quickly.
why: The noodles cooled by themselves, so the resulting state is 冷めている.

jp: シャツのボタンが{外[はず]れています|tr-teiru-tearu}よ。
en: Your shirt button has come undone.
why: The button came undone accidentally and is now in that state, so 外れている.

jp: 部屋[へや]を涼[すず]しくするために、窓[まど]を{開[あ]けてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: To keep the room cool, I have opened the window and left it that way.
why: Someone opened it on purpose (を), and the state remains, so the transitive 開けてある.

jp: 壁[かべ]に大[おお]きな地図[ちず]が{貼[は]ってある|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: A big map has been put up on the wall.
why: Someone stuck the map up on purpose and it stays there, so 貼ってある; 貼る has no intransitive partner.

jp: 黒板[こくばん]に、今日[きょう]の予定[よてい]が{書[か]いてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Today's schedule has been written on the blackboard.
why: Someone wrote it and the writing remains for people to read, so 書いてある.

jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に、母[はは]のメモが{置[お]いてある|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Mother's note has been left on the desk.
why: Mother put it there deliberately and it stays, so 置いてある; 置いている cannot take が.

jp: 窓[まど]の外[そと]に、洗濯物[せんたくもの]が{干[ほ]してあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Laundry has been hung out outside the window.
why: Someone hung the laundry out on purpose and it is there now, so 干してある.

jp: 玄関[げんかん]に、きれいな花[はな]が{飾[かざ]ってある|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Beautiful flowers have been arranged in the entrance hall.
why: Someone arranged the flowers and they remain on display, so 飾ってある.

jp: 夜[よる]、暗[くら]くならないように、玄関[げんかん]の電気[でんき]を{つけてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: So that it isn't dark at night, the entrance light has been left on.
why: Someone switched the light on for a purpose (を), and it stays on, so つけてある.

jp: 誰[だれ]でも入[はい]れるように、ドアの鍵[かぎ]を{開[あ]けてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: So that anyone can come in, the door has been left unlocked.
why: Someone unlocked it deliberately (を object), and it stays that way, so 開けてある.

jp: パーティーのために、テーブルを{並[なら]べてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The tables have been set out for the party.
why: Someone arranged the tables on purpose (を), and they stay arranged, so 並べてある.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]の日[ひ]を、来週[らいしゅう]の月曜日[げつようび]に{決[き]めてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The date of the meeting has been set for next Monday.
why: Someone decided the date on purpose (を), and the decision stands, so 決めてある.

jp: 寒[さむ]いと思[おも]って、部屋[へや]の暖房[だんぼう]を{入[い]れてある|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Thinking it would be cold, I have turned on the heating in the room.
why: I switched it on in preparation (を), and it is running now, so 入れてある.

jp: 重[おも]い荷物[にもつ]を、先[さき]にホテルに{届[とど]けてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: I have had the heavy luggage sent ahead to the hotel.
why: I arranged the delivery in advance (を object), so the transitive 届けてある.

jp: 燃[も]えるごみを、玄関[げんかん]に{出[だ]してあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: I have put the burnable trash out at the entrance.
why: I put the trash out for collection (を object), and it is waiting there, so 出してある.

jp: お客[きゃく]さんが来[く]るので、玄関[げんかん]にスリッパを{並[なら]べてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Guests are coming, so I have lined up slippers in the entrance.
why: I arranged the slippers for the guests (を), and they are ready, so 並べてある.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]の中[なか]に、新[あたら]しい映画[えいが]の広告[こうこく]が{貼[は]ってあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: An advertisement for a new movie has been put up inside the train.
why: Someone posted the ad and it remains in place, so 貼ってある; 貼っています cannot take が.

jp: 子供[こども]が食[た]べられるように、肉[にく]を小[ちい]さく{切[き]ってあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: So that the child can eat it, I have cut the meat small.
why: I cut the meat on purpose (を), and it is ready, so 切ってある.

jp: 箱[はこ]に、送[おく]り先[さき]の住所[じゅうしょ]が{書[か]いてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: The destination address has been written on the box.
why: Someone wrote the address on the box and it stays there, so 書いてある.

jp: いつでも入[はい]れるように、お風呂[ふろ]を{洗[あら]ってあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: So that you can get in any time, I have already cleaned the bath.
why: The cleaning is already done in preparation, so 洗ってある; 洗っています would mean washing now.

jp: 部屋[へや]に、お客[きゃく]さんのためのお茶[ちゃ]が{置[お]いてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Tea for the guests has been set out in the room.
why: Someone set the tea out in advance and it is there now, so 置いてある.

jp: 車[くるま]のトランクに、非常用[ひじょうよう]の水[みず]が{積[つ]んである|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: Emergency water has been loaded into the trunk of the car.
why: Someone loaded the water as a precaution and it stays there, so 積んである.

jp: 台風[たいふう]が来[く]るので、窓[まど]を全部[ぜんぶ]{閉[し]めてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: A typhoon is coming, so I have closed all the windows.
why: I closed them on purpose (を) and they stay shut, so the transitive 閉めてある.

jp: 遅刻[ちこく]しないように、時計[とけい]を五分[ごふん]{進[すす]めてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: So that I won't be late, I have set my clock five minutes fast.
why: I moved the clock ahead deliberately (を), and it stays set, so 進めてある.

jp: 暑[あつ]いので、ジュースを冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]で{冷[ひ]やしてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: It's hot, so I have chilled some juice in the fridge.
why: I chilled the juice on purpose (を), and it is ready to drink, so 冷やしてある.

jp: 壁[かべ]に、家族[かぞく]の写真[しゃしん]を{掛[か]けてある|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: I have hung a photo of my family on the wall.
why: I hung the photo myself (を object) and it stays up, so the transitive 掛けてある.

jp: 手紙[てがみ]には、もう切手[きって]が{貼[は]ってあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: A stamp has already been put on the letter.
why: Someone already stuck the stamp on and it is in place, so 貼ってある.

jp: 行[い]きたい店[みせ]には、地図[ちず]に印[しるし]を{つけてあります|tr-teiru-tearu}。
en: I have marked the shops I want to visit on the map.
why: I made the marks on purpose (を object), and they remain, so つけてある.
